data.narrative:
Stratolaunch is a private-stage space and aerospace company operating in a sector comprising 5 public comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Two standard valuation approaches were evaluated. Peer-median anchoring was inapplicable: while 14 same-sector peers exist, filtering by stage, adjacency, and valuation tier yielded fewer than three datapoints—the minimum threshold for reliable median-based inference. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples was also inapplicable. The Space & Aerospace sector median P/S stands at 26.4x across the 6 public tickers identified; however, Stratolaunch's revenue is not on file, precluding any revenue-based multiple application. Private companies in this sector rarely disclose sufficient operational metrics to support comparable valuation methods.

This analysis cannot support a quantitative valuation range given the absence of both (i) a sufficiently dense peer set at matching stage and tier, and (ii) disclosed revenue or comparable financial metrics for the target. A credible valuation would require either direct access to Stratolaunch's financial performance, or expansion of the data set to include additional same-stage space-tech peers with disclosed metrics. Valuation in this context remains dependent on deal-specific diligence and management guidance rather than market-derived multiples.
